title: Per-route retention hierarchy with sampled evidence bundles and residency-aware exports
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a per-route retention hierarchy that lets customers declare TTLs for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics independently, with an automated sampled-evidence export workflow that is residency-aware and verifiable (hash-chains + signed bundles). Provide admin UI/HTTP APIs to preview retention footprint and to request certified evidence packages for legal/compliance needs.
background: Customers increasingly demand fine-grained control over how long different artifacts (prompt text, generated responses, request metadata, and aggregated metrics) are retained. Existing retention feature work has been focused on top-level TTL templates and bulk exports; this ticket scopes a combined UX + runtime enhancement: per-route overrideable retention hierarchy, a sampled evidence generation pipeline that produces cryptographic proofs of content at time-of-export, and residency-aware packaging so exported bundles respect tenant region and legal boundaries.
scope:
- API and Console: per-route retention settings (prompt, response, request log, metrics) with inheritance from tenant templates; retention preview showing estimated storage delta and monthly cost impact.
- Export: sampled-evidence job that collects a configurable percentage of requests per-route over a time window and emits an export bundle with hash-chain, manifest, and signed provenance metadata.
- Residency: export runner honors tenant residency (region tagging) and only stores/exports artifacts to allowed destinations.
- Runtime: lightweight tagging in request pipeline to mark TTL and sampling eligibility; background archival & deletion workflow.
- Audit: generated export contains chain-of-custody fields for compliance reviewers.
out_of_scope:
- Long-term cold-archive tooling (S3 lifecycle policies are separate).
- Full-text de-identification or PII redaction algorithms (we will provide hooks for transformer-based redactors in a follow-up).
- Dedicated (reserved) customer on-prem package adjustments (private deployment policy differences handled in separate PM ticket).
proposed_solution:
1) Data model: extend route configuration with 4 TTL fields (prompt_ttl, response_ttl, request_log_ttl, metrics_ttl) and a sampling policy (rate/% or stratified).
2) Console: single page to edit route-level TTLs with clear inheritance from tenant template, and a 'Preview retention footprint' modal that simulates 7/30/90-day storage using recent traffic stats.
3) Export pipeline: scheduled sampled-evidence jobs per-tenant that: - collect sampled records, - compute per-record SHA-256, - chain-records into a manifest with timestamps, - sign manifest with service key, - produce a zip bundle with protobuf-compatible manifest.json and proof.sig.
4) Residency enforcement: export runner validates destination against tenant residency constraints and uses regional temporary storage; any cross-region export requires explicit tenant admin approval.
5) APIs: Admin REST endpoints to trigger ad-hoc evidence exports, preview retention impact, and retrieve signed bundle metadata.
6) Security: Key rotation plan and KMS integration for signing.
7) Telemetry: track exported bundle counts, size, latency, and sampling coverage metrics for SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route TTL fields available in API and Console and can override tenant defaults
Retention preview accurately estimates delta within ±15% using sampled traffic data and matches billing dashboard for a pilot tenant
Scheduled sampled-evidence job produces signed bundles with manifest and SHA-256 hashes validated by an internal verification tool
Export runner enforces tenant residency: bundles for EU tenants are created in EU regions and cannot be exported to non-EU destinations without admin approval
Background deletion job respects per-record TTLs and publishes deletion events to audit log within 5 minutes of completion
Admin API returns bundle metadata including chain root, signer id, and sample coverage percentage
success_metrics: Enablement: 30% of new routes created in pilot tenants configured with per-route TTLs within 8 weeks
Compliance ops: Reduce manual evidence bundling tickets by 80% for pilot customers
Accuracy: Retention preview estimates within ±15% for 90% of tested routes
Performance: Export job median completion time < 10 minutes for 24-hour sampled window (pilot scale)
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Design and API contract finalized (POST /admin/routes/{id}/retention, POST /admin/exports)
Week 3-4: Engineering spike + prototype sampled-evidence job with local signer (eng spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1712)
Week 5-7: Console UI and retention preview, internal QA with two pilot tenants (legal and payments teams)
Week 8-9: Security review, KMS signing integration, and performance tuning of export runner
Week 10: Soft launch to pilot tenants with opt-in; gather feedback and adjust sampling defaults
Week 12: General availability behind feature flag; create migration guide and admin docs
risks: Sampling trade-off: too low sampling % undermines evidentiary value; too high increases storage/cost
Export size and runtime: large volumes could blow past SLA if not sharded and region-local
Legal variance: different jurisdictions may require greater provenance than current manifest design; will need legal review
Security: private keys for signing must be protected; any compromise undermines trust in evidence bundles
